# Resource SVM

Activates an existing QoS Policy for an existing SVM.

## Related ONTAP commands

```commandline
* vserver modify -qos-policy-group
```

## Supported Platforms

- On-prem ONTAP system 9.6 or higher
- Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

## Example Usage

This applies the policy group `performance-svm02` to SVM `svm02`

```terraform
resource "netapp-ontap_svm_qos_policy_activation" "example" {
  cx_profile_name = "cluster4"
  svm = {
    name = "svm02"
  }
  qos_policy = {
    name = "performance-svm02"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->

## Argument Reference

### Required

- `cx_profile_name` (String) Connection profile name
- `svm` (Attributes) SVM to manage (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--svm))
- `qos_policy` (Attributes) QoS policy group to apply to the SVM (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--qos_policy))

<a id="nestedatt--svm"></a>

### Nested Schema for `svm`

Optional:

- `name` (String) The name of the SVM
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the SVM

<a id="nestedatt--qos_policy"></a>

### Nested Schema for `qos_policy`

Optional:

- `name` (String) The QoS policy group name
- `id` (String) The QoS policy group UUID

## Import

This resource supports import, which allows you to import existing activated QoS Policy for SVM into the state of this resource.
Import require a unique ID composed of the SVM name, and connection profile, separated by a comma.

id = `svm_name`,`cx_profile_name`

### Terraform Import

For example

```shell
 terraform import netapp-ontap_svm_qos_policy_activation.example svm02,cluster4
```

!> The terraform import CLI command can only import resources into the state. Importing via the CLI does not generate configuration. If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the import block instead.

### Terraform Import Block

This requires Terraform 1.5 or higher, and will auto create the configuration for you

First create the block

```terraform
import {
  to = netapp-ontap_svm_qos_policy_activation.import
  id = "svm02,cluster4"
}
```

Next run, this will auto create the configuration for you

```shell
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf
```

This will generate a file called generated.tf, which will contain the configuration for the imported resource

```terraform
# __generated__ by Terraform
# Please review these resources and move them into your main configuration files.
# __generated__ by Terraform from "svm02,cluster4"
resource "netapp-ontap_svm_qos_policy_activation" "import" {
  cx_profile_name = "cluster4"
  svm = {
    name = "svm02"
  }
  qos_policy = {
    name = "performance-svm02"
  }
}
```
